difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 220-222: the type of n-types is an (n+1)-type. The proof (source lines 223-234) is short but carries the whole argument and is not visible in the statement: it unfolds what an identity in the universe of n-types is, replaces it by the type of equivalences through the mere-proposition character of being an n-type, then chains two reductions, first through the embedding of equivalences into function types and then through the preservation of n-type-ness under arrow types, and finally treats the boundary case n equal to minus two, where the same argument gives a (-1)-type and inhabitedness of the equivalence type upgrades it to a (-2)-type. The two reduction steps and the boundary case are the substance; the statement alone shows none of them.
